item.title: Ohio man charged over graphic threats to kill Trump, behead GOP lawmaker
item.description: The FBI arrested an Ohio man who allegedly sent graphic death threats to Jewish Republican Rep. Randy Fine and President Donald Trump via email.
item.content:encoded:
An Ohio man was arrested by the FBI after allegedly making graphic threats against a Jewish Republican congressman and calling for the death of President Donald Trump.

Alex Justin Miller, 26, is accused of sending a "true threat" to Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., and his family, according to the Department of Justice (DOJ). 

A copy of the message separately obtained by Fox News Digital shows Miller allegedly called Fine and his family "Nazi f—-s" and said he would burn their house down, pledging he would "never stop until your head is hanging from the rooftops of the White House." His message ended with "DEATH TO RANDY FINE AND DEATH TO DONALD TRUMP."

Miller was charged with interstate transmission of a threat to injure by the U.S. Attorney in the Middle District of Florida and faces up to five years in prison if convicted, the DOJ said.

FAA EMPLOYEE CHARGED WITH ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL PRESIDENT TRUMP IN EMAIL TO WHITE HOUSE

The incident was investigated by the FBI and the Brevard County Sheriff's Office with assistance from the Secret Service and Capitol Police, the DOJ said.

"It was so graphic. It says, 'I'm gonna murder you. I'm going to cut your head off. I won't stop,'" Fine told Fox News Digital. "I reported it immediately. I unfortunately have learned what the difference is between a nasty message and a death threat, and this clearly was a death threat."

The full message read: "Dear fat--- piece of s---stain, I cannot wait to take a trip to you lovely home and light the whole place on fire and murder you and your entire family in the middle of the night while you sleep. I hope you disgusting Nazi f---s sleep with one eye open for the rest of your life because I will NEVER stop until your head is hanging from the rooftops of the White House. You deserve 10000% to be beheaded and have your body paraded through the streets. DEATH TO RANDY FINE AND DEATH TO DONALD TRUMP!!" 

Fine said he received the threat via email on the morning of primary Election Day in the Sunshine State. He also said it reinforced his belief that federal officials need more protection.

"I don't know what this person's motives were for writing this, but it's someone not from Florida. So, you know, this was not a local constituent that was upset," he said. "I do think members of Congress need more security than we oftentimes get."

FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL TRUMP, RUBIO AND BONDI

He added that law enforcement found and arrested the man within 36 hours.

"I'm incredibly grateful to the U.S. attorney, the FBI, the Capitol Police, and all the law enforcement in Florida who took this seriously. The bottom line is, don't do this. Don't write messages like this to elected officials, Republican or Democrat. You want to call us bad people? Be my guest, but do not do this sort of thing," Fine said.

item.title: I feared AI would leave my community behind. Now I see a path to prosperity
item.description: The AI boom demands 130,000 additional skilled trades workers by 2030, creating massive opportunities for electricians, plumbers and HVAC technicians.
item.content:encoded:
There has been worry of late that AI may eliminate jobs. I have seen the power of AI, and I can understand why some sectors are worried.  I have even worried that this ongoing AI revolution may leave behind the troubled youth in my South Side of Chicago neighborhood. For the past several years, I have been building this massive Leadership and Economic Opportunity Center to teach young people the trades as a way out of poverty and violence. And I’m sitting here, wondering if I made a mistake. Have I created something that is outdated? I admit I felt this panic deep within my soul. Was I handing my youth a caveman tool when they needed the latest technology?

I wondered how we would adapt to this ever-changing world that changes so fast that sometimes I can’t even remember who was in the news last week. So I took a walk through the walls of the new building. It’s beautiful. It brings me such joy to see the rooms and the promises of opportunity that come with them. We have rooms for the trades in every aspect of construction, from wood cutting to plumbing. We have rooms for creating new electricians. We’ve also got rooms for creating HVAC workers and fiber technicians, and more. We’ve got amazing equipment for our youth to train on. But was all of this for nothing? Did time pass us by?

I did not create this building to leave another empty shell on the South Side of Chicago. Just down the street from us, Walgreens and McDonald’s fled, and there are boarded-up buildings. There are no grocery stores, and we’re a true food desert where fried foods are often our only quick and easy option. The rates of homeownership here are abysmal. Despite low home prices, some blocks have homeownership rates as low as 14% to 24%. We have a poverty rate of 40% to 51%, depending on which block you go to. And don’t even get me started on our local schools.

DIVINE PURPOSE HELPED BRING CHICAGO’S MOST-DANGEROUS BLOCK BACK TO LIFE

That is why I am so desperate to bring a symbol of hope to my community through the building of this community center. I still felt that quiet desperation as I walked past the construction workers at work. I came upon a young man who had finished his job here. After thanking him for his contribution, I asked him where he was going next. He explained that he had secured work for a major AI manufacturing facility in a nearby township. As he told me more and more, I thought to myself: There’s a building boom.

When we think of AI, we think of the Silicon Valley story about white-collar workers. The media is full of headlines about white-collar workers afraid of losing their jobs. But at the same time, I was also noticing, in my layman’s view of the world, that AI could potentially be the wealth-of-knowledge generator that places practical expertise directly in the hands of young people failed by the current systems. In other words, AI could help my youth leapfrog gaps in local schooling and training by enabling self-sufficiency faster.

THE AI REVOLUTION THREATENS OFFICE JOBS, BUT REVIVES DEMAND FOR SKILLED TRADES

I also began, thanks to my conversation with the young construction worker, to see that many people were missing the big opportunity here. While AI may transform or eliminate certain desk jobs, it is also a world unto itself that must be built. We’re talking about data centers, power grids, fiber networks and advanced manufacturing facilities. 

Who is going to help build this revolution? I looked down from the roof of my community center at the young people on the sidewalks and prayed that it would be them and their peers.

This AI boom will require, for many years, electricians, HVAC technicians, construction workers, plumbers, pipefitters, fiber technicians and other skilled tradespeople. I recently drove out to see some of these facilities being built, and they’re massive. The world is changing before our eyes, and we’re entering an entirely new era of infrastructure.

A SOUTHERN STATE JUST TOOK THE TOP SPOT IN ONE OF THE WORLD’S FASTEST-GROWING INDUSTRIES

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has called this the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Major tech companies are projected to spend roughly $700 billion this year alone on AI-related facilities. This will only increase as more and more of us adopt AI. And it is happening as hundreds of data centers are under construction or planned across the United States. One analysis estimates the nation will need 130,000 to 140,000 additional skilled trades workers by 2030 just to support AI infrastructure—before accounting for housing, hospitals and energy projects competing for the same talent.

This demand has created an urgency to develop new workers. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects electrician employment to grow 9% from 2024 to 2034, a rate much higher than average. The bureau projects about 81,000 openings each year. HVAC mechanics and installers are projected to grow 8 percent, which translates to roughly 40,100 openings annually. Plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters are expected to see about 44,000 openings per year. 

WANT TO STRENGTHEN AMERICA'S ECONOMY? THE KEY INVESTMENT IS HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT

In May 2026, the construction industry reported approximately 298,000 job openings. Specialty-trade contractors already employ more than 565,000 electricians and 349,000 plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters. The Associated Builders and Contractors estimates the industry needs roughly 349,000 net new workers in 2026 alone. In data-center hotspots, skilled-trades wages already carry a 7 percent premium overall, with plumbers and pipefitters seeing gains as high as 20 percent.

More importantly, the median annual pay for these jobs is solid, at around $62,000 to $72,000. This may not seem like a lot, but for a kid who has known nothing but generational poverty, this is the way out of the culture of dependency. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Yes, one job like this can end that vicious, soul-sucking cycle that has kept so many of us stuck in the permanent Black underclass. These careers build assets, they restore dignity and pride, and they give people a stake in America.

At first, I feared that the AI revolution would leave my youth behind. But now I’m more convinced than ever that this is the greatest opportunity to come along.

I was part of the Great Migration myself, the very tail end of it. My mother and her husband moved from a tiny town in Tennessee to Muncie, Indiana, for better jobs in industrial factories. When I visited them and later moved to Indiana, I was exposed to a world of more opportunities. 

I see this cycle of life coming back around today, and I’m determined more than ever to push my youth onto this AI opportunity wagon. As they say, this is their chance to strike it rich in America.

item.title: ‘Send help’: LA GOP leader issues desperate appeal after Dem mayor’s campaign vid shocks viewers
item.description: LA County GOP Chair Roxanne Hoge says Karen Bass's viral 6-to-1 matching funds video reveals how Democrats codified electoral 'shenanigans' into law.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Los Angeles County GOP Chair Roxanne Hoge issued an impassioned appeal for Republicans to "send help" to Democratic-controlled California, describing what she sees as rampant corruption in the state and saying most people "can't understand the level of obsession they have with controlling our lives."

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Hoge addressed the online reaction to a recent viral video posted by Democratic Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass in which the mayor said the city government would match six times every dollar donated to her re-election campaign. While some social media users expressed shock, Hoge said she was not surprised.

"The rest of the country doesn't understand what we're living under here," she told Fox News Digital.

"The number one thing people need to understand about Los Angeles in particular and California in general is that they've codified all of their shenanigans," she explained. "What normal people consider cheating or weirdness in the electoral process? It's all in the rules [here]."

LOS ANGELES PROPOSAL TO ALLOW NONCITIZENS TO VOTE IN LOCAL ELECTIONS SPARKS ONLINE BACKLASH

In a recent viral social media post, Bass, Los Angeles’ 72-year-old progressive mayor, said that "when you donate to our campaign, the city can match your donation 6 to 1," adding, "If you donate $5, the city turns it into $35."

Bass said that "thanks to LA’s super match program, every qualified donation from Los Angeles residents is matched six to one by the city." She added that after this year’s mayoral primary, in which Republican candidate Spencer Pratt garnered significant support, "we had to start over from scratch."

"So, we need you to rush in your matching donation right now, to help fuel this campaign," she said.

Social media users questioned and criticized Bass’ comments.

Conservative activist Billboard Chris commented, "How is it legal to take money from Los Angeles taxpayers to fund your own re-election campaign?" Commentator Matt Van Swol wrote, "Can someone please explain to me like I’m 5 years old how this is not COMPLETELY illegal?????"

KAREN BASS RIPPED AFTER SUGGESTING TAXPAYER-FUNDED DENTAL CARE FOR METH USERS

Author Michael Shellenberger simply wrote, "This is grotesque."

"Is this a JOKE?!?" wrote well-known Los Angeles doctor and political commentator Houman David Hemmati. "Why on EARTH are LA City taxpayers, who can’t even afford to clean up their streets or have water in their fire hydrants, forced to match contributions to Bass’ Mayoral reelection campaign 6:1?!? … HUH?! Insanity!"

Hoge, however, said the matching-funds program Bass describes in her campaign video is legal under city law. Los Angeles voters approved a public campaign-financing system in 1990 that the City Council later expanded into today’s six-to-one matching-funds program. Donations are subject to caps and eligibility rules.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"Voters passed something that sounded so good; they always sound so good at the beginning. Public financing matching funds for campaigns on a one-to-one basis. That seems great, right?" she said. "And then it transmogrifies … into what we have today, this many-headed hydra of insanity where taxpayers are on the hook for $6 for every dollar raised by a city of L.A. candidate."

She noted that the rule applies not only to mayoral campaigns but also to City Council campaigns, adding that they "Have many active [Democratic Socialists of America] members currently sitting and running."

Hoge said "the message that Karen Bass is sending is the same message that those of us who live here behind the blue curtain have been getting for decades."

"And that is, ‘Forget it, Jake, it's Chinatown. Don't try to go against City Hall,’" she said.

SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES'

"We saw Spencer Pratt mount a very strong argument for sanity and good governance. It wasn't partisan, what he was saying. It was pure common sense, and they rose up because they were threatened."

Fox News Digital reached out to Bass’ campaign and office for comment.

Despite California’s political landscape, Hoge urged Republicans not to write off America’s most populous state as a lost cause.

"California is totally worth fighting for because it is an absolute gem," she said, adding, "We are living with people who gleefully would reach into the shower and change the temperature while you're having a bath."

Addressing Republicans directly, she said, "We belong to the leave me alone party."

"California, being in the west, is the ultimate place where you should be free to write your own story. And that, I think, is the number one thing people have to remember," she said. "They need to send help."

item.title: Outgoing House Democrat Al Green files another impeachment resolution targeting President Donald Trump
item.description: Democratic Rep. Al Green of Texas, who lost a Democratic primary runoff earlier this year, filed a new resolution targeting President Donald Trump for impeachment.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Al Green, D-Texas, who has repeatedly targeted President Donald Trump for impeachment, renewed his effort by filing a new impeachment resolution on Monday.

"Our country and the lives of people within it are at risk as President Donald John Trump is a great threat to the United States democratic republic, its Constitution, and democracy, violating Article II, Section 1, Clause 8 of the United States Constitution and its mandate to faithfully execute the office of President of the United States and, to the best of his ability, preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution of the United States," the document declares.

The resolution accuses Trump of "abusing the powers of the presidency by operating United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) as his vicious, quota-driven, unaccountable paramilitary police forces, transgressing with anonymity and secrecy, assaulting people, committing and covering up unjustified killings of civilians (including Renée Good, Alex Pretti, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero) with impunity (acting as judge, jury, prosecutor, and executioner), terrorizing communities, and brazenly and wantonly devolving the United States democratic republic into an authoritarian regime, where unjustified killings and coverups by ICE and CBP are normalized."

AL GREEN RESPONDS TO JULY 4 QUESTION WITH RENEWED CALL TO IMPEACH TRUMP

In a statement provided to Fox News Digital on Tuesday, White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said, "This type of garbage is contributing to our law enforcement officers facing a more than 1,300% increase in assaults against them. The brave men and women of ICE and CBP put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists. Al Green should be thanking President Trump and our law enforcement for delivering the largest decrease in violent crime in American history."

Fox News Digital also reached out to the Department of Homeland Security, ICE and CBP on Tuesday.

Given that Republicans currently hold the majority in both chambers of Congress, his latest impeachment push likely won't succeed.

REP. AL GREEN TELLS HOMELAND SECURITY SEC. MULLIN TO 'SHUT UP' AFTER CALLING HIM A RACIST AT HEARING

But in a letter to the president, Green said, "Mr. President, I am well aware of the fact that you will be defended by persons who will say, ‘The House won’t impeach, and if it did, the Senate won’t convict.’ Sir, my response is that articles of impeachment that are not approved by Congress can express on-the-record disapproval of presidential actions and demonstrate that there are some of us watching and willing to act."

Green has fielded impeachment resolutions multiple times across both of Trump's White House terms.

The congressman, who has served in the House since 2005, lost a Democratic primary runoff to Rep. Christian Menefee in May.

TRUMP COULD FACE IMPEACHMENT IF DEMOCRATS SEIZE HOUSE MAJORITY, GOP LEADER WARNS

The House impeached Trump twice during his first term, but in both cases, the Senate vote did not meet the threshold necessary for conviction. The Senate's vote on the second impeachment took place after Trump had already departed from office.

item.title: 3 things Democrats don’t want you to know about AI and data centers
item.description: AI data centers are reviving small towns like Ellendale, N.D., bringing jobs, tax revenue and lower electricity bills to communities left behind.
item.content:encoded:
Everywhere you look, people are talking about artificial intelligence (AI). It’s on your TV. It’s on your radio. It’s on your social media feed. And it seems like Democrats and their media allies are doing their very best to scare you away from it by telling you that AI is going to destroy the environment, take your job and hike up your utility bills. But anytime Democrats and liberal journalists are in lockstep on an issue, that should set off your alarm bells – why do they want you to be scared?

The reason is that left-wingers want to seize control of AI for their own political purposes. But don’t take my word for it. As Democratic strategist Jesse Ferguson put it: "the fight for Democrats is not ‘we are for AI’ or ‘we are against AI.’ That framing is a trap. The fight is over control."

AI HAS AN OPINION AND IT USUALLY LEANS LEFT. YOU HAVE A RIGHT TO KNOW ITS AGENDA

THE NEXT AMERICAN BOOM COULD BE HERE — UNLESS WASHINGTON REGULATES IT TO DEATH

AI and data centers are revitalizing the pro-Trump small towns that make up the heartbeat of America – the exact small towns that were left for dead when offshoring hollowed out the American manufacturing industry.

Take Ellendale, N.D., for example. Decades of economic decline left the town with barely 1,000 residents as of the most recent census. As the school superintendent put it: "We were a dying little town." But then a data center arrived – and everything changed.

META OFFERS PAID TRAINING FOR AI DATA CENTER JOBS

That’s not a one-off story. In Louisiana’s Richland Parish – a community that voted for President Donald Trump by a nearly 40% margin in 2024 – a Meta data center brought in so much tax revenue that local teachers received bonuses of $50,000.

A SOUTHERN STATE JUST TOOK THE TOP SPOT IN ONE OF THE WORLD’S FASTEST-GROWING INDUSTRIES

Or consider rural Virginia’s Louisa County, where data center development didn’t just bring jobs – it brought tax cuts, too, thanks to the surge in tax revenue from the data centers. And then there’s the little red town of Quincy, Wash., where an investment surge from data centers has brought a new $120 million high school, a 79% decrease in the poverty rate, new sidewalks, more police officers on the beat, property tax cuts and more.

In short: the total revival of the town. So, it’s no surprise that Wells Fargo analyst Ohsung Kwon’s research concluded that communities with data centers are seeing "significant economic benefits" – both during data center construction and for years afterwards.

Nobody is telling you the truth about water, utility bills and what data centers have to do with them. Not the electric companies, not the liberal media and certainly not elected Democrats like New York Democrat Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

THE REAL REASON YOUR ELECTRIC BILL IS SOARING THIS SUMMER WILL SURPRISE YOU

The power companies were quick to scapegoat data centers for cost increases that began well before the very first version of ChatGPT was released on Nov. 30, 2022. But in case there was any doubt, President Donald Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Plan guarantees that AI companies pay their own way, ensuring that Americans are protected from rate increases due to data center developments. More than 80% – and counting – of Americans are covered under the Ratepayer Protection Plan.

In some cases, data center developments can actually lead to lower bills for neighboring residents. A June 2026 study found that data center developments indeed led to modest decreases in electricity rates. That might seem counterintuitive at first, but the reality is that electric companies have huge fixed costs – costs that they have to pay whether they have one customer or one million – in which case having a massive customer (data centers) absorb the lion’s share of those fixed costs means fewer costs to spread among everyone else.

THE BIGGEST THREAT IN AMERICA'S RACE WITH CHINA ISN'T BEIJING, TECH EXECUTIVE WARNS

Reality bears this out as well. In Ellendale, N.D., electricity bills were $250 lower per customer thanks to their new data center. Who wouldn’t want an annual $250 discount on their electric bill?

The narrative about water use might be the most misleading one of all. It’s largely due to a bestselling book – "Empire of AI" – that was so factually flawed that it suffered multiple corrections. Even the Washington Post observed that Empire of AI’s calculations were off by a "thousandfold."

DEMOCRATS SOUND ALARM OVER AI JOB APOCALYPSE — BUT LABOR MARKET ISN'T FOLLOWING SCRIPT

And not only was the book wrong, but it quickly became outdated, too, because data centers are moving to closed-loop cooling systems in which "day-to-day cooling doesn’t depend on adding water" and "community water usage for cooling the data center is effectively zero." Or, as Nvidia’s chief sustainability officer put it: "The water consumption challenge for data centers is largely solved."

For decades, America’s biggest companies have enjoyed an enormous built-in advantage: They can afford armies of programmers, analysts, marketers, lawyers and consultants that small businesses simply can’t. AI is leveling the playing field for small businesses by giving them access to the same arsenal of weapons at a fraction of the cost.

So, it’s no wonder that Russell Kaplan, the president of Cognition AI, said he’s anticipating "an explosion in small businesses" thanks to the AI revolution. But don’t take his word for it: small business owners themselves tell a similar story. The Small Business Cash Flow Trend Report found that 61% of small-business owners report using AI, with 91% of those users reporting a positive impact on their business.

It’s not just small-business owners, either. Blue-collar workers are seeing a jobs boom thanks to AI – and these jobs are paying better, too. "Dirty Jobs" host Mike Rowe recounted in a podcast interview how, when he visited a data center in Plano, Texas, he was stunned by the wealth that was flowing to blue-collar workers. "The electricians that I interviewed and met two months ago in a data center in Plano, Texas, all under 30 years old, all making $240,000 to $280,000 a year, all with as much overtime as they want," Rowe said. Everybody wins when the American worker succeeds – everybody except socialists who depend on keeping people poor.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The world is changing pretty quickly. There’s no doubt about that. But the next time somebody tries to scare you into opposing American AI dominance, ask yourself three questions: 1) Who is trying to make you feel that way? 2) Why do they want you to feel that way? And 3) Are they telling you the truth?

The answers to those questions will reveal a lot.

item.title: California sheriff doubles down on seizing ballots as state Supreme Court hears whether he must return them
item.description: Sheriff Chad Bianco still holds 650,000 seized ballots as the California Supreme Court weighs whether he must return them to state officials.
item.content:encoded:
Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco remains defiant as the California Supreme Court deliberates whether he has to return approximately 650,000 ballots he seized from a November 2025 special election on redistricting.

The court heard arguments Monday from Bianco’s lawyers and from California, where state Attorney General Rob Bonta launched a legal challenge to Bianco’s ballot seizures in March, ordering him to return the ballots.

Bianco, however, refused, arguing through his legal team that he had a legal obligation to investigate the ballots after receiving a complaint.

"I did this, and this was legal," Bianco told reporters. "I went a different route. They are legal. Both routes are legal. It's just their side doesn't like the route I chose."

DOJ DEMANDS 865K DETROIT BALLOTS, THREATENING POSSIBLE LEGAL ACTION

Bianco is still holding the ballots, his lawyer Bradley Hertz told reporters Monday, arguing that they are evidence.

CALIFORNIA ACCUSED OF BLOCKING FEDERAL VOTER ROLL AUDIT AS DOJ ESCALATES PROBE OF ELECTION FRAUD CLAIMS

"The sheriff is holding that evidence, safeguarding it as a custodian for the court," Hertz said.

The ballots are from a November 2025 special election in which state voters decided on Proposition 50, a legislative redistricting measure that passed by more than 3.4 million votes, according to the California Secretary of State.

CALIFORNIA ELECTION LIMBO FUELED BY 4 PRESSURE POINTS DRAGGING OUT VOTE COUNT, EXPERT SAYS

Bianco, however, appeared to question whether the official count was valid.

"How strange, that now we have evidence that the machines counted something different than the ballots that we have, and an Attorney General runs in to stop that investigation so that we’ll never know," Bianco said outside the courthouse.

CALIFORNIA DOGE LEADER SLAMS NEWSOM, BONTA OVER STATE’S MASSIVE FRAUD ISSUES: "EVERY DAY IS OPPOSITE DAY"

In filing his March legal challenge to Bianco’s ballot seizures, Bonta joined the UCLA Voting Rights Project, which launched a separate legal challenge to Bianco’s actions.

"This is a sheriff that – despite the clear language in the California constitution, and in California government code, providing me direct supervision, authority over him – failed to comply with it," Bonta told reporters outside the courthouse Monday.

"He can read, he knows what it says, it makes his violations even more egregious," Bonta also said.

Bianco, for his part, challenged Bonta’s interpretation of California code. "If you take it word for word, in that context, it means that he has direct authority that if I’m not doing my job he can order me to do it and if I don’t do it he can do it for me. But he cannot stop an investigation."

Fox News Digital contacted the UCLA Voting Rights Project, the Riverside County Sheriff's Office and the California Attorney General's Office for further comment.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump taunts Canada on renaming Lake Ontario the 'Lake America' amid rising border trade rift
item.description: Trump floats renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake America" and accuses Mark Carney of fabricating claims about French-language demands in trade talks.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump escalated his war of words with Canada on Tuesday morning, floating a U.S. push to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" and accusing Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney of lying about the Trump administration's position on French-language protections.

"The United States is giving serious consideration to changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in that we don’t expect to [sic] doing much business with Ontario any longer," Trump wrote Tuesday morning on Truth Social.

Trump followed with another broadside aimed directly at Carney, rejecting claims the U.S. had sought concessions affecting the French language during the countries' recently collapsed trade negotiations.

A POPULAR COCKTAIL HAS A TRUMP TRADE PROBLEM YOU PROBABLY DIDN’T KNOW ABOUT

"I would never interfere with Canadians speaking French!" Trump wrote. "In fact, I have never even thought of doing such a stupid thing."

"This lie was made up by a weak and ineffective Prime Minister in an attempt to gain political support, which he has totally lost, from the people of Quebec," Trump added. "I love French Canadians!"

The posts marked the latest escalation in an increasingly bitter dispute between Washington and Ottawa after trade negotiations broke down late last week, triggering a new round of tariffs and threats of retaliation between the longtime allies.

OPINION: TRUMP MUST CLOSE THE BACK DOOR CHINA USES TO EXPLOIT NORTH AMERICAN TRADE

"We were not prepared to compromise on the protection of the French language and our culture," Carney said Saturday while announcing the suspension of negotiations, adding that those issues were "never on the table" for Canada.

Carney doubled down Monday while in Quebec, arguing that French-language protections viewed by the U.S. as trade irritants were fundamental rights in Canada. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, however, disputed Carney's characterization, calling the French-language dispute a "funny, fake story" and saying the U.S. objection instead centered on requirements affecting American streaming companies.

Ontario is Canada's most populous province and a key hub in the tightly integrated U.S.-Canadian auto industry. Lake Ontario is shared by Ontario and New York, making Trump's proposed name change another provocative shot at America's northern neighbor as the economic standoff deepens.

TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED

The president has previously used geographic names to make a political point, ordering the change of Gulf of Mexico to be called Gulf of America.

Vice President JD Vance traveled to Maine on Monday and delivered a lengthy defense of the administration's hard-line approach toward Canada, accusing Ottawa of treating Chinese goods more favorably than products coming from its American neighbor.

"They treat Chinese goods more fairly than they do the goods that come from the people of Maine: It’s insanity," Vance said during a question-and-answer session Monday in Brewer. "And what we’ve said to Canada is stop it."

Vance said the two countries had appeared close to an agreement before negotiations fell apart, blaming Canadian officials for bringing what he described as unreasonable demands to the table at the last minute.

Trump separately announced Monday that 50% tariffs on Canadian automobiles, auto parts, trucks and steel would take effect Jan. 1, 2027, accusing Canada of years of unfair treatment of American producers.

"Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years," Trump wrote Monday.

Despite the sharpening rhetoric, Vance left open the possibility Monday that Washington and Ottawa could eventually return to the negotiating table.

"I think that we should have a deal," Vance said. "We expect fairness in our trade policy."

item.title: Callaway admits it approved controversial Good Good woman-shoving ad in late-night statement
item.description: Callaway CEO Chip Brewer admitted the company approved the Good Good golf ad showing Garrett Clark shoving a woman before it was posted online.
item.content:encoded:
Callaway Golf has issued a second statement regarding the controversial advertisement with Good Good, this time admitting that it greenlit the since-deleted video showing a man shoving a woman to the ground.

Good Good, the popular YouTube golf channel that boasts more than 2 million subscribers, teamed up with Callaway for a special edition driver. In the advertisement promoting the golf club, Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark shoved member Alexis Miestowski to the turf.

The beginning of the advertisement focuses on Miestowski reaching for the driver in a golf bag. Seeing this, Clark sprints at her, shoves her to the ground with his forearms, and stands over her before saying, "Do not touch my new driver."

FRUSTRATED BUBBA WATSON CONFRONTS UNRULY FAN AT LIV GOLF INDIANAPOLIS IN INTENSE SCENE

After deleting the video from its social channels, Good Good apologized in a statement, explaining that the ad "ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand." Following Good Good's apology, Callaway shared a statement of its own explaining, "We are disappointed by the content that was posted, and are appreciative of Good Good for addressing this. We look forward to working together to ensure a more inclusive space in golf."

As questions continued to be asked about how the advertisement made it past production and was ultimately published online, Callaway CEO Chip Brewer released a statement just after 1 a.m. ET on Tuesday morning, owning up to the fact that the company approved the video before posting.

"Last week, Good Good Golf and Callaway posted a video to promote a co-branded driver. While the video was produced by Good Good, it was approved by Callaway prior to posting. That approval should never have happened. Mistakes were made, and we are taking the matter very seriously," the statement began.

"As we deal with the consequences of our mistake and complete our investigations, I want to make it clear that we sincerely apologize for the video. The content was inappropriate and does not reflect our values. To be clear: We are unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence, or threatening behavior of any kind.

"As soon as we recognized the seriousness of the issue, it was escalated appropriately, and the video was immediately removed. Preliminary statements were issued by both Good Good and Callaway, and now this statement has followed. We are also conducting both internal and external investigations and have already made changes to our approval processes aimed at ensuring this will never happen again.

"We believe we have been a positive force for diversity and inclusion in the game of golf. This video was completely inconsistent with that. I assure you that we will learn from this and do better."

OutKick has reached out to Good Good for further comment and will update this story if there is a response.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

The PGA Tour commented on the advertisement amid the backlash that Good Good received online.

"The PGA Tour believes in golf’s ability to bring people together and create a welcoming environment for all," the statement said. "We do not condone violence in any form, and the since-deleted video does not reflect our values or commitment to inclusivity and respect."

The PGA Tour stepping into the situation is noteworthy, with Good Good sponsoring the Tour's inaugural Good Good Championship this November in Austin, Texas.

item.title: Could Iran’s regime collapse? Experts assess Bessent’s bid to sever financial lifelines
item.description: Scott Bessent's "Economic D-Day" against Iran sent the rial to an all-time low as experts debate whether maximum pressure can trigger regime change.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s Monday announcement that America will impose the economic equivalent of the military campaign that defeated Nazi Germany on the Islamic Republic of Iran could set off a series of events leading to the dissolution of the nearly 47-year-old dictatorship in Tehran, according to Iran experts.

Bessent’s declaration of economic warfare follows President Donald Trump’s commitment last week to launch an "economic D-Day" against the Tehran regime. The comprehensive U.S. economic pressure point campaign targeting Iran’s already troubled economy could have dramatic effects on the restive population in the country of over 90 million people.

"In the Second World War, D-Day marked the historic beginning of a campaign with our allies to target and drive the enemy from its positions, including those in third countries. Today, in that same spirit, we are launching an economic onslaught against Iran's financial connections around the globe," said Bessent. He added, "Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone. Iran's fanatics devote themselves to death to America and seek nuclear weapons to do just that. They have murdered and maimed more of our citizens and service members than any other terrorist regime on Earth."

TRUMP THREATENS 'UNPRECEDENTED' ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES FOR ANY NATION AIDING IRAN

Just hours before Bessent spoke, Iran’s currency, the rial, plunged to an all-time low. The rial fell to 2.02 million to the U.S. dollar. Iranians are struggling to afford basic goods.

Jonathan Harounoff, an Iran expert and British author of Persian heritage, told Fox News Digital that "Ultimately, this pressure campaign will likely continue to cripple the regime and set the stage for perhaps yet another domestic uprising. The precise timing of such a revolt is impossible to predict."

Harounoff, who has written extensively on upheavals in Iran against the clerical leadership, added, "What isn't impossible to predict is that the regime is governing brutishly over a repressed population that has endured sustained economic and social immiseration. It's only a matter of time before more protests break out, and the real question is whether international organizations like the U.N. and Western governments will choose to stand by — or tangibly support the Iranian people and actively sever any cooperation they maintain with the regime."

LEAKED IRAN REPORT FINDS RECORD PUBLIC ANGER AS REGIME FOCUSES ON HOLDING POWER

He warned that, "Too often, outsiders speak of regime change as if it were a passive exercise. Certainly, only the people of Iran can bring about organic, homegrown, transformational change — and they have 47 years of turmoil and repression driving them toward it. But there are real ways to support the Iranian people (Starlink, supporting think tanks and foundations, raising awareness of the plight of Iranians, etc.) and help them achieve what has, until now, been a quixotic dream."

Jason Brodsky, policy director at United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), told Fox News Digital, "The question is often asked: what makes this iteration of the maximum pressure campaign different from all other iterations? The answer is this iteration is taking place against a backdrop where there is a synchronization of economic and military pressure against the Iranian regime — a combination which has never been deployed by a U.S. administration until now. The U.S. naval blockade currently in place against Tehran is unprecedented. The Iranian regime's industrial base — for example, steel plants — has also been damaged following kinetic strikes. The Iranian regime’s military capacity has likewise been degraded."

IRAN ACCELERATES EXECUTION CAMPAIGN AGAINST ANTI-REGIME ACTIVISTS AMID INTERNET CENSORSHIP

He noted, "So Operation Economic Outcast is being launched at a time of true weakness in terms of its national power. The regime's risk tolerance may be increasing, but so is its desperation. The drivers pushing the Iranian people into the streets to protest have only gotten worse since January — with political, economic and social forces all deteriorating. The regime is seeking to use the tussle over the Strait of Hormuz as a distraction from all of this."

Alireza Nader, an independent Iran expert, however, expressed skepticism that the tightening of the economic screws could provoke a mass revolt. "I don’t think starving the civilian population in Iran will lead to an American victory. The regime has demonstrated an extreme brutality toward the population, having massacred thousands of unarmed protestors this past January. And Iranians are less likely to rise up when the promised help to them from Trump and Netanyahu never materialized."

Nader said, "The Woman, Life, Freedom movement against the regime prior to the war had the best chance of overthrowing the regime. This war has disrupted the Iranian people’s struggle for freedom."

Beni Sabti, an Iran expert at the Institute for National Security Studies (INSS) in Israel, told Fox News Digital that "there are some protests inside Iran for pensioners and those who did not get their salaries."

He said the January protests began with "economic problems." President Trump has said that the Iranian regime murdered 52,000 Iranian demonstrators during the Jan. 8 and 9 mass protests against the regime.

Sabti, who was born in Tehran and has deep sourcing in Iran, said Trump’s economic offensive campaign against Iran could "bring out the people again." He said there were some "rumors" that lower-rank army soldiers did not receive their salaries.

The U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent seized on the point that the regime will have payroll problems today. He said, "To the ordinary soldiers supporting this regime, as more and more of your paychecks stop or are supposedly just delayed, ask whether your commanders are leading your country to triumph or to ruin, and recall that the Berlin Wall fell when ordinary soldiers decided not to shoot at their own people."

item.title: New evidence in Lockerbie Pan Am Flight 103 bombing case pushes federal judge to postpone trial
item.description: A federal judge delayed the Pan Am Flight 103 bombing trial after defense attorneys said prosecutors handed them new evidence over the weekend.
item.content:encoded:
The criminal trial of a former Libyan intelligence official charged in the 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 was postponed by a federal judge Monday after defense attorneys said they received new evidence over the weekend from prosecutors.

Jury selection was set to begin Wednesday in Washington, D.C., in the trial of Abu Agila Mohammad Mas’ud Kheir Al-Marimi. It would have been the first U.S. trial stemming from the bombing that killed 270 people, most of them Americans.

U.S. District Judge Dabney Friedrich did not specify the nature of the novel evidence in his order.

Al-Marimi’s defense team said prosecutors handed them the evidence on Saturday, adding in their request to the judge that their "constitutional and ethical obligations require the defense to investigate this development."

LONG-LOST PAN AM CRASH WRECKAGE FOUND DECADES AFTER DEADLY DISASTER THAT RESHAPED AIRLINE SAFETY

The judge granted Al-Marimi’s lawyers the delay and scheduled a status hearing on Sept. 1.

Al-Marimi is charged with making the bomb that downed the Pan Am flight, killing all 259 passengers and crew members. The plane came down over the small town of Lockerbie, Scotland, where it destroyed an entire city block and killed 11 people on the ground.

Citizens of 21 countries were among the victims, including 190 Americans and 43 people from the United Kingdom. Among those aboard were 35 Syracuse University students returning home from a semester abroad.

The bomb exploded less than 40 minutes into the flight, which had departed from London Heathrow Airport and was headed to John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York City.

CUBAN EX-PRESIDENT RAUL CASTRO INDICTED ON CHARGES INCLUDING MURDER, CONSPIRACY TO KILL US NATIONALS

Kara Weipz, board president of the nonprofit Victims of Pan Am Flight 103, told The Associated Press that her organization has not received any details about what caused the delay in Al-Marimi’s trial.

Weipz’s brother, Richard Monetti, was one of the Syracuse students who died on the flight.

Weipz said the families of the victims had already been packing to head to Washington for the trial.

"At the same time, for almost 38 years we've been seeking the truth of what happened," Weipz said. "If that's what this is, then that's a good thing, and this delay is worth it... It's important to hear all the facts."

FBI BRINGS IRAQI MAN ACCUSED OF COORDINATING NEARLY 20 TERROR ATTACKS IN EUROPE TO FACE TRIAL IN NEW YORK

Prosecutors say Al-Marimi carried out the bombing at the behest of Libyan dictator Muammar Qaddafi, who was ousted from power in 2011 and violently killed by rebels.

In 2000, two other Libyan agents were tried by a panel of Scottish judges on a U.S. military base in the Netherlands. One was convicted, while the other was acquitted.

For decades, the true identity of the bombmaker has been a mystery.

Al-Marimi, now in his mid-70s, faces two counts of destruction of an aircraft resulting in death. He could be sentenced to life in prison if convicted.

Prosecutors say Al-Marimi worked for Libya’s intelligence service from roughly 1973 until 2011, eventually attaining the rank of colonel.

Investigators allege he brought a suitcase containing a bomb to an airport in Malta and handed it off to co-conspirators for a flight to Frankfurt, Germany. The suitcase was then transferred to London, where it was loaded onto Flight 103.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Mysterious 3,000-year-old hoard with violently smashed sword emerges during construction project
item.description: Metal detecting led archaeologists to a Bronze Age hoard of deformed sickles, a shattered sword blade and ingots deposited in a flooded Czech Republic wetland.
item.content:encoded:
Archaeologists in Central Europe recently came across an unusual hoard of Bronze Age tools — including a sword that had been deliberately smashed with a powerful blow.

The discovery was announced by Archaeological Center Olomouc (ACO), a research institution in the Czech Republic, on August 12. The hoard was found in a heavily flooded area at the end of May.

The cache, discovered near Kojetín in central Moravia during archaeological work connected to a railway project, contained an assortment of worn and broken bronze objects.

MYSTERY DEEPENS AFTER 2,700-YEAR-OLD BRONZE SWORD EMERGES STANDING UPRIGHT

The artifacts included eight deformed sickles, one intact sickle, part of a sword blade, ornament fragments, three ingots and two unfinished objects.

"Use-wear analysis has shown that most of the bronze objects had been used before their deposition and that some were deliberately damaged," ACO officials said in a statement.

Pictures show the mud-covered Bronze Age artifacts shortly after their discovery. 

The sword bore particularly dramatic signs of damage, with archaeologists concluding that it had been struck apart with a single powerful blow.

"[It was] probably delivered with a chisel or an axe, while several of the sickles were intentionally deformed," the ACO release read.

1,740-YEAR-OLD ROMAN COIN BEARING EMPEROR'S NAME FOUND AS ENGLAND RAIL DIG REVEALS CLUES

Lead archaeologist Vít Záhorák told officials the team's decision to use metal detection was crucial to finding the objects.

"We knew our work was continuing in an area occupied by an extensive prehistoric settlement, so we also used metal-detecting survey during the archaeological monitoring," said Záhorák.

"It was this method that led to the discovery of the bronze hoard," he added. 

While it may seem plausible that the tools were concealed as a temporary hiding place, officials say the evidence points to a more ceremonial purpose.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"The current interpretation instead suggests that the objects were deliberately deposited in a former wetland and that their deposition may have formed part of a ritual practice," the statement said.

Officials noted that the Kojetín discovery has parallels with other Bronze Age sites.

"Deposits of bronze objects in watery or waterlogged settings are also known from other Bronze Age sites," the statement read.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"In some of these cases, archaeologists have considered a possible connection with ritual practices. Further specialist analyses will help determine whether the Kojetín hoard had a comparable significance."

The artifacts are currently undergoing conservation and analysis by specialists.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Bronze Age hoard is far from the only archaeological discovery to emerge in the Czech Republic in recent years.

Last year, officials announced the discovery of multiple military graves during highway construction, including one dating back to the 1745 Battle of Žďár during the Second Silesian War.

This spring, ACO officials reported finding over 1,000 ancient artifacts spanning during excavations along a future high-speed railway route.

item.title: Charles Barkley declares WNBA is 'for women only' after ongoing transgender athlete debate
item.description: Hall of Famer Charles Barkley declared the WNBA is "for women only" and criticized Adam Silver and Cathy Engelbert for not addressing the issue earlier.
item.content:encoded:
NBA Hall of Famer and sports commentator Charles Barkley declared Monday that the WNBA is "for women only. Period."

During an interview on CNN host Michael Smerconish's podcast, Barkley commented on former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom being removed from a WNBA game Sunday night after being confronted by Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud. Critics have accused Freedom of deliberately stirring up controversy by wearing a T-shirt that read "WOMAN noun. adult human female."

Barkley responded that while he respects the transgender community, he believes "under no circumstances" should biological men play against biological women and criticized NBA and WNBA leadership for failing to address that.

WNBA HAS 'NO IDEA WHAT THEY'RE ABOUT TO FACE,' ENES KANTER FREEDOM SAYS AS LEAGUE TAKES ON TRANS ATHLETE ISSUE

"I'm disappointed in [NBA commissioner] Adam Silver and Cathy [Engelbert] the [WNBA] commissioner," Barkley said. "First of all, you can't let stupid stuff go out to the internet, which is one of the worst things that ever happened to the world. They should have come out two weeks ago before all this. People are looking for attention now...but [Freedom] has a point though, because Cathy and Adam haven't said, 'Hey, it's in the title, WNBA."

Barkley urged the commissioners to come out and draw a line in the sand, saying, "'There's no transgender people going to play in the WNBA. If you don't like it, kick rocks. And we're not going to discuss it anymore.'"

"And Enes is trying to get attention," Barkley continued. "'No, we're not doing that either. The WNBA is for women. And listen, this is the last time we're going to discuss it. We're not going to turn it over to the fools on the internet. We're not going to turn it over to Congress and things like that. The WNBA is for women only. Period.'"

Barkley added that between stories like Freedom's removal from a game and the backlash against Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham opposing biological males in female sports, the WNBA is gaining a bad reputation.

CLAY TRAVIS PLEDGES $10M FOR ‘BATTLE OF THE SEXES’ MATCHUP AS WNBA TRANS DEBATE INTENSIFIES

"When's the last time you heard something positive about the WNBA? I can't even remember. And I'm a WNBA fan," Barkley said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the NBA and WNBA for comment.

Jennifer Sey, founder and CEO of XX-XY Athletics, praised Barkley's comments for speaking "the truth" out loud to his audience.

"Elite athletes have always known the truth about sex and sports. Charles Barkley is just bold enough to say it out loud," Sey said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Independent Women ambassador Payton McNabb agreed with Sey, telling Fox News Digital, "It really is that easy to say. If the WNBA wants this conversation to go away as badly as they claim, then stop dancing around it and stand up for women. Say the league is for women, period. What are they so afraid of? They continue to create this controversy for themselves by refusing to say something that should be so simple. Charles Barkley had no problem saying it - why does the WNBA?"

COMEDIAN DECLARES HUGH LAURIE 'CAN'T BE CANCELED' AS ACTOR COMES TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM'S DEFENSE

Director of Independent Women's Law Center May Mailman, however, expressed doubts that Barkley's comments would sway public responses to protecting women's sports.

"Men should not play in women’s sports, and everyone knows what that means. The real question is whether Barkley speaking up will give others confidence to do so. And unfortunately, it’s hard to see that, because Sophie, after many years, got the confidence to do so, and she’s nearly had her head taken off at games and has fans showing up to protest her," Mailman said.

The WNBA came under controversy after both Freedom and former NBA player Royce White declared their intentions to join the WNBA in response to the players and coaches supporting transgender players.

Though the sports league's rules state that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA," the WNBA rules do not define what a "woman" is.

item.title: AI may answer some New Orleans 911 calls
item.description: New Orleans 911 uses Carbyne AI to triage repeat auto crash calls, but strict limits keep human call-takers in control of all other emergencies.
item.content:encoded:
Calling 911 is one of those moments when you expect a human voice on the other end. In New Orleans, though, an artificial intelligence system may answer in a limited situation involving certain calls about already reported auto crashes.

The Orleans Parish Communication District handles 911 emergency communications in Orleans Parish. OPCD says the AI helps manage repeat crash reports while keeping human call-takers available for other emergencies.

Hearing an automated voice after dialing 911 could make anyone pause. So, here is what the system actually does, when it steps in and where humans remain in control.

New! Free live CyberGuy class: Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats

Join us Saturday, Aug. 29, at 10 a.m. ET for a free CyberGuy LIVE class covering five simple steps to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will explain how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. You’ll also receive our financial protection checklist, and every registrant will get a link to the class recording afterward.

Reserve your free spot today at CyberGuyLive.com.

SMART STREET SENSORS COULD BE WATCHING YOUR CITY NEXT

OPCD began working with emergency communications company Carbyne on AI-assisted call triage before launching the system in 2023. Carbyne calls the technology AI-V Emergency Call Triage. The company designed it to help emergency communication centers deal with sudden floods of calls about the same event.

A car crash can create that problem quickly. OPCD says one accident can generate numerous calls from nearby drivers. During busy periods, those repeat reports can pile up while call-takers handle other emergencies. The AI gives OPCD another way to manage some of those repeat calls.

The system checks whether an incoming call comes from within 200 meters, or about 650 feet, of a crash that 911 already knows about. It can step in only when every human call-taker is occupied. OPCD says it has not deployed the system this way for any other category of 911 call.

The conversation starts simply. OPCD says the AI identifies the call as New Orleans 911. It then asks whether you are calling about an accident at a specific location. Your response determines what happens next.

Answer anything other than yes, and the system returns your call to the 911 queue for a human call-taker. OPCD says this safeguard works regardless of the language you use. Confirm that you are calling about the known crash, and the AI tells you that 911 already knows about it.

Someone involved in the accident or a caller with more information can stay on the line for a human. Otherwise, the system tells the caller that they may hang up. OPCD says the AI itself cannot end the call. The caller decides when to hang up.

The limits of the system become especially important when you are talking about 911. OPCD says the AI cannot dispatch emergency responders. It also cannot determine how urgently a call should be handled.

Its role focuses on identifying this specific type of repeat crash call and determining whether the caller needs to remain in the human queue.

OPCD also says the technology isn’t a large language model like ChatGPT. The system performs a much narrower task within the emergency communications network. Comparing it directly with a general-purpose AI chatbot can therefore create the wrong impression of what it actually does.

This was one of my first questions about the technology. OPCD says the system sends a call back to the queue or a human operator when it cannot understand the caller.

It also defaults to a human when a call falls outside the limited crash scenario it was designed to handle. The system supports multiple languages. OPCD also trained it using local 911 recordings to better understand New Orleans accents and local street names. That local training can help in a city where a street name could challenge an unfamiliar voice system.

AI CHATBOT PRIVACY: WHAT YOUR AI MAY KNOW ABOUT YOU

There is another safeguard worth knowing about. OPCD says the AI system keeps the 911 center's normal callback procedures in place.

Once your call enters the queue for a human, hanging up does not erase it. The call center can contact you after staff work through the queue. Still, OPCD advises callers to stay on the line whenever possible. A call waiting in the queue will eventually reach a call-taker.

An AI interaction does not disappear from the system. OPCD says it logs these calls with the normal metadata and audio recording. Those records remain available when investigators need them.

The agency also says calls handled through the system do not get uploaded to an outside large language model. That addresses an obvious privacy question whenever AI becomes part of an emergency communications system.

OPCD says it tested the technology for several months before putting it into live use. The agency says its team reviewed 100% of the calls handled by the system during its first three months. During that review period, OPCD says it found no false positives or false negatives.

In practical terms, the system handled the calls OPCD expected it to handle without taking over calls outside its intended use. That result is encouraging, although it covers a defined review period rather than every call handled since the system launched. OPCD says its compliance team continues to audit the technology closely.

Carbyne has published performance figures from its work with OPCD. Because Carbyne provides the technology, these numbers are vendor-reported rather than findings from an independent study. In a Carbyne case study, the company says its AI-V Emergency Call Triage system triaged more than 3,500 events during a 90-day period.

Carbyne reports that redundant calls among those triaged calls dropped by more than 30%. The company also says distressed callers got their calls answered up to 40 seconds faster on average. Those numbers suggest the approach has potential. Still, I would like to see OPCD continue releasing its own performance data over time.

OPCD says no. The agency has struggled to fill all of its available call-taker positions. Staffing shortages also remain a broader problem across the 911 industry. OPCD says it views AI as a tool to support its human call-takers rather than replace them.

For New Orleans, the goal is to reduce repeat crash reports during call surges so human call-takers can reach other people waiting for help. The agency says it has not expanded AI triage to other categories of 911 calls.

OPCD is studying what else the technology might eventually do. However, those experiments are taking place in a testing environment rather than on the live 911 system.

The agency says it has explored whether AI could help with other types of call clusters. It has not put those uses into operation. OPCD also says it will not expand the AI triage tool to additional 911 categories unless the agency can ensure the technology works properly. For now, its live use remains focused on the specific auto-crash scenario.

New Orleans may be the test case here, but this story reaches far beyond one city. AI is starting to move into public services that people rely on during emergencies. That means your community could eventually face the same questions. When should AI step in? What should it be allowed to handle? How quickly can you reach a human when something goes wrong?

For now, New Orleans keeps the system on a very short leash. It handles only certain repeat calls about known crashes, and human call-takers remain available for anything outside that narrow use. The bigger question is what happens next.

As more emergency centers look for ways to handle staffing shortages and call surges, AI could become part of the conversation where you live. If that happens, you should know exactly what the system can do, what it cannot do and how easily you can reach a person. That is what I would be watching most closely.

LAGUARDIA AIRPORT AI HOLOGRAM ANSWERS TRAVELER QUESTIONS

Hearing AI on a 911 call would make a lot of people uneasy. I understand why. In an emergency, you want help fast and a clear way to reach a person. New Orleans has given its AI a narrow job. It can help filter repeat reports of an accident that 911 already knows about while human call-takers are busy. I can see the benefit. One crash may generate many calls while someone elsewhere needs help with a completely different emergency. Still, 911 deserves an extremely high standard. OPCD says its early audit found no false positives or negatives, and the agency continues to monitor the system. I want that scrutiny to continue. Any move beyond this limited use should come with clear safeguards and solid performance data.

Would you feel comfortable hearing an AI system after dialing 911 when it could help human call-takers reach other emergencies faster, or would you always want a person to answer first? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Sarah Spain says WNBA players need ‘real media,’ but that sounds more like league-approved PR
item.description: Sarah Spain wants the WNBA to steer players toward "real media" she trusts, but credential denials and tone policing reveal a league loyalty test.
item.content:encoded:
Sarah Spain thinks the WNBA should steer its players toward what she calls "real media."

That’s a PR job. Not a journalism job.

MEGAN RAPINOE CALLS ON TRADITIONAL WNBA MEDIA TO BE REPLACED WITH THOSE WHO ‘UNDERSTAND QUEER CULTURE’

On a recent episode of her podcast, Spain said she wants the league to keep setting up relationships with "the real media" that covers the WNBA "in a fair way."

Her definition of fair is pretty clear. Players trust the outlet, the outlet helps build their brands and the WNBA helps make the relationship happen.

She’s laying out a league-approved list of "reporters" players are supposed to trust.

The people who don’t make it? Spain threw them in with "a rando" on the internet spreading "bulls---."

And, by the way, Spain’s already inside the system she wants the league to grow. Spain's podcast has recently featured Connecticut Sun assistant coach Roneeka Hodges, Golden State Valkyries guard Veronica Burton, Seattle Storm players Dominique Malonga and Awa Fam, WNBA legends Cheryl Swoopes and Ticha Penicheiro, and former WNBA president Donna Orender.

Spain has the access and she calls that fair coverage. Then she says the WNBA should help its players find more outlets like hers.

That's convenient, huh?

The WNBA has publicists, marketers, agents, sponsors and social media teams to build brands. It doesn't need to turn reporters into another arm of that operation.

Spain’s preferred media setup is already taking shape in the WNBA.

I know because the teams have put it in writing.

The Atlanta Dream denied an OutKick credential request for its Aug. 5 game against the Phoenix Mercury. In follow-up answers, the Dream said it had denied 14 applications, given priority to season credential holders and outlets that consistently cover the team, and considered "the tone of coverage."

Tone of coverage.

That has nothing to do with whether a reporter got facts wrong. It has everything to do with whether the team likes the way it is being covered.

WOMEN’S SPORTS MEDIA OUTLET BACKS TRANS ATHLETES, THEN AVOIDS QUESTIONS FROM REPORTER WHO DISAGREES

The other credential denials use different words, but the same record keeps pointing in one direction.

The Dallas Wings said priority went to outlets that regularly cover the Wings and WNBA. The Connecticut Sun cited "reputable media/wire services" and outlets with a record of covering the organization. The Las Vegas Aces said it would prioritize local outlets and organizations that regularly provide editorial coverage of the Aces and WNBA.

The Chicago Sky asked a Fox News reporter about his planned coverage, denied the request and said credentials were for media covering games "for basketball purposes."

Then Atlanta told us it weighs tone.

That’s the one that matters.

The WNBA can call the preferred outlets reputable. Spain can call them real media. But a credential decision based on tone is still a team deciding whether it likes the reporter doing the coverage.

And the league just gave us another example.

When it wanted the public to know Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White were ineligible for the 2027 draft, the WNBA didn’t answer OutKick’s questions about the rule it used. Instead, unnamed league sources told Front Office Sports the men were ineligible and called their declarations "simply publicity stunts."

Front Office Sports printed the conclusion and the league’s framing. But it never told readers whether it asked the WNBA to define "woman," explain its eligibility standard or say how Freedom and White failed it. If it did ask, readers were never told the WNBA refused to answer.

That’s different from the treatment OutKick gets when we report something inconvenient for the league. Then Front Office Sports wants documentation, competing sources and a discussion about our motives.

Spain says the WNBA should steer players toward "real media" outlets they can trust. The league has already made clear which outlets it trusts: the ones that will carry its message without making it answer the question.

LEFT-WING SPORTS HOST SARAH SPAIN LAUNCHES DISGUSTING PERSONAL SMEAR OF SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM

USA Today columnist Christine Brennan asked DiJonai Carrington whether she intentionally poked Caitlin Clark in the eye during the 2024 WNBA playoffs. It was a question that had to be asked after an incident happened on the court, yet the WNBA Players’ Association responded by calling for Brennan to lose her access.

Spain has gone after Brennan, too. Earlier this summer, she called Brennan’s Caitlin Clark coverage a "dereliction of duties as a journalist" and questioned whether Brennan’s book promotion explained her singular focus on Clark.

In Spain’s version of "real media," the reporters who ask the wrong questions don't belong.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Then Sophie Cunningham said "biological men" shouldn't compete in girls’ and women’s sports. Days later, the WNBA’s biggest players and Commissioner Cathy Engelbert were available all weekend in Chicago for All-Star festivities.

The questions should have been obvious to any reporter interested in doing their job.

Do you agree with Cunningham? Does the WNBA support female-only sports? What is the league’s policy on transgender eligibility?

The reporters with access didn’t ask.

Spain had access, too. She moderated a panel at the WNBA’s All-Star Media & Innovation Summit, hosted a live show, sat courtside at the game and later said she spoke with Paige Bueckers, Fever coach Stephanie White, Stephanie Dolson and Aliyah Boston.

Her All-Star recap had plenty about the parties, cookies, mascots and her baseline seat. It didn't include a single question about Cunningham’s comments, female-only sports or the WNBA’s transgender eligibility rules.

And when Fever coach Stephanie White read a prepared statement accusing unnamed people of hate, fear mongering and divisiveness, WNBA media elevated the rehearsed rant into an "important" moment instead of testing a single one of those claims.

Spain predictably took White’s side, too. She played part of White’s performative outrage speech on her podcast, said she was "adamantly opposed to Sophie Cunningham’s grift" and said White "was warranted in that anger and frustration."

Spain wants the league steering players toward outlets that will help build their brands and tell them who to trust. Those are the outlets she calls "real media."

The reporters who ask questions the league doesn’t want answered get hit with a credential denial, accused of having the wrong tone or brushed off as "randos."

That isn’t fair coverage.

It’s a loyalty test that punishes the reporters who are actually doing their jobs.

item.title: Major brain changes that occur around age 50 could impact dementia risk
item.description: Microglia decline after age 50 as inflammatory blood-derived immune cells infiltrate the hippocampus, potentially driving neuroinflammation and dementia.
item.content:encoded:
The brain may undergo a notable shift at midlife, as new research suggests that its protective immune cells begin to decline and are increasingly replaced by inflammatory cells at around age 50.

Researchers from the University of California, San Diego; New York Genome Center; and University of California, Irvine, found that these brain changes may help explain why aging increases the chances of neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative disease, including dementia.

The study analyzed postmortem tissue from the hippocampus – the portion of the brain that is responsible for learning and memory – in 40 neurologically healthy adults, ranging from 20 to 95 years of age.

THE 'AGE' OF YOUR BLOOD COULD PREDICT DEMENTIA RISK, NEW STUDY SUGGESTS

"The most striking change was that after about age 50, the brain’s resident immune cells, called microglia, appear to be increasingly replaced by immune cells that enter from the bloodstream," first author Nathan Zemke, Ph.D., principal investigator at the UC San Diego Center for Epigenomics, told Fox News Digital.

"Microglia normally protect the brain by clearing debris and responding to injury, but the incoming cells carry stronger inflammatory signals."

The researchers believe this shift may contribute to chronic inflammation linked to cognitive decline and neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s.

They also noted the deterioration of cells involved in maintaining the blood-brain barrier – the protective filter that helps keep harmful substances out of the brain – as well as widespread changes in DNA and gene activity.

'LONGEVITY GENE' MAY PROTECT THE BRAIN FROM ALZHEIMER'S BY BOOSTING DNA REPAIR, STUDY FINDS

One of the most exciting implications of the study, according to Zemke, is that the replacement immune cells originate in the blood, which means they are more accessible than cells already deep inside the brain.

"It may eventually be possible to modify blood-derived immune cells so that they are more protective and less inflammatory when in the brain," he said. "That could provide an entirely new way to approach Alzheimer’s and other neurological diseases without having to directly manipulate cells within the central nervous system."

Although these findings are still in early stages, Zemke said, gaining a better understanding of why this immune-cell replacement happens – and why it happens earlier in some people than others – could lead to new strategies for preserving brain health during aging.

The study’s chief limitation is that it studied human brain tissue collected postmortem from different individuals across the adult lifespan, the researchers noted.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"That allows us to identify strong age-related patterns, but it cannot directly show how the same person’s brain changes over decades or prove that a particular cellular change causes cognitive decline or Alzheimer’s disease," Zemke said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"We also do not yet know what triggers the influx of blood-derived immune cells into the brain. Determining whether changes in the blood-brain barrier, inflammation, genetics, lifestyle or other factors initiate this process will be an important next step."

The researcher emphasized, however, that he would not recommend that people make any specific medical or lifestyle changes based on this study alone. 

"These findings are primarily about understanding the biology of brain aging and identifying new directions for prevention and treatment," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The timing and extent of the brain changes varied considerably between individuals, suggesting that brain aging is not necessarily a fixed process that happens identically in everyone.

"The next challenge is to understand what drives that variation and whether some of those factors can be modified," Zemke added.

The study also included a small sample of just 40 people and examined tissue only from the hippocampus, meaning the findings may not reflect immune changes throughout the entire brain.

The study, which was funded by the National Institutes of Health, was published in the journal Science.
